Partial responses can still be useful

A range fetch may stop before the closing tags arrive, but the parser can still recover a document tree. The extractor should retain complete paragraphs that were received before the byte limit.

The caller records that the capture was bounded and can schedule a full fetch when quality is too weak. It should not crash merely because an article, body, or html element is left open.

This final paragraph is intentionally cut in the middle so the fixture resembles a real bounded response whose last network chunk ended before the document was complete
